title: Cardiovascular Comprehensive Set 1: Integrative Responses (Short answer)

questions.prompt: What is the primary initiating hemodynamic event when a person move quickly from a supine to a standing position?
questions.modelAnswer: Venous pooling in the lower extremities due to the high compliance of veins.

questions.prompt: Define orthostatic hypotension in the context of postural changes.
questions.modelAnswer: A decrease in arterial blood pressure upon standing, often causing light-headedness or fainting.

questions.prompt: Why does stroke volume initially decrease when an individual stands up?
questions.modelAnswer: Due to decreased venous return (reduced preload).

questions.prompt: During the compensatory response to standing, what specific change occurs in the firing rate of the carotid sinus nerve?
questions.modelAnswer: The firing rate decreases due to decreased stretch on the carotid sinus.

questions.prompt: List the four primary consequences of the baroreceptor reflex that attempt to restore mean arterial pressure (P_a) during a postural challenge.
questions.modelAnswer: (1) Increased heart rate, (2) increased contractility, (3) arteriolar constriction (increased TPR), and (4) venoconstriction (increased venous return).

questions.prompt: In the context of the "central command" of exercise, what changes occur in the autonomic outflow to the heart?
questions.modelAnswer: Increased sympathetic outflow and decreased parasympathetic outflow.

questions.prompt: Explain why the total peripheral resistance (TPR) decreases during aerobic exercise despite increased sympathetic activity.
questions.modelAnswer: Because of vasodilation of arterioles in the exercising skeletal muscle caused by local vasodilator metabolites (lactate, K^+, adenosine).

questions.prompt: What mechanical mechanism, other than venoconstriction, helps increase venous return during physical activity?
questions.modelAnswer: The "muscle pump" (mechanical squeezing of veins by contracting skeletal muscle).

questions.prompt: Why does pulse pressure typically increase during strenuous exercise?
questions.modelAnswer: Because stroke volume increases.

questions.prompt: Describe the effect of exercise on the arteriovenous (A-V) O_2 difference and the physiological reason for this change.
questions.modelAnswer: It increases because the tissues extract and consume more oxygen from the blood.

questions.prompt: Which two major vascular beds are "spared" from the selective arteriolar vasoconstriction directed by the central command during exercise?
questions.modelAnswer: The coronary and cerebral circulations.

questions.prompt: What is the initiating event in the cardiovascular response to an acute hemorrhage?
questions.modelAnswer: Loss of blood volume, which decreases mean systemic pressure.

questions.prompt: How does the body compensate for the loss of blood volume through "autotransfusion" at the capillary level?
questions.modelAnswer: Arteriolar vasoconstriction decreases capillary hydrostatic pressure (Pc), which favors the absorption of fluid from the interstitium.

questions.prompt: Which specific hormonal system provides the slow, long-term compensation for blood volume loss after a hemorrhage?
questions.modelAnswer: The renin-angiotensin II-aldosterone system.

questions.prompt: What are the two distinct effects of Antidiuretic Hormone (ADH) via its V_1 and V_2 receptors during the response to hemorrhage?
questions.modelAnswer: V_1 causes arteriolar vasoconstriction; V_2 increases water reabsorption in the renal collecting ducts.

questions.prompt: How does the baroreceptor reflex affect venous compliance during a state of shock?
questions.modelAnswer: It decreases venous compliance (venoconstriction) to increase venous return and stressed volume.

questions.prompt: Explain the "Bainbridge reflex" and distinguish it from the baroreceptor reflex response to high arterial pressure.
questions.modelAnswer: The Bainbridge reflex is an increase in heart rate in response to increased venous/atrial pressure (sensing volume excess), whereas the baroreceptor reflex decreases heart rate in response to increased arterial pressure.

questions.prompt: What is the role of Atrial Natriuretic Peptide (ANP) when the cardiopulmonary baroreceptors sense an increase in blood volume?
questions.modelAnswer: It causes vasodilation (decreased TPR) and increased Na^+ and water excretion by the kidneys.

questions.prompt: In the steady state of moderate exercise, what is the typical change in mean arterial pressure, and how is this achieved?
questions.modelAnswer: It shows a slight increase; the large increase in cardiac output is mostly balanced by the decrease in TPR.

questions.prompt: Why does the heart rate increase during a hemorrhage even though blood volume is low?
questions.modelAnswer: The decrease in arterial pressure is sensed by baroreceptors, triggering a reflex increase in sympathetic activity and decrease in parasympathetic activity to the SA node.
